display.purpose: --text-bill-xl, 3.6rem. The title in the desktop programme note and the single largest thing on screen. Archivo wdth 62 / wght 900, line-height 0.86, uppercase via the bill-title utility.

headline.purpose: --text-bill-lg, 2.6rem. The phone's TONIGHT heading, the phone hero title, and the empty-library headline.

title.purpose: --text-bill-md, 2.15rem. Every bill entry title, plus the zero-match and read-failure headlines. Deliberately larger than a card this size would normally carry: the name is the entry.

section.purpose: --text-bill-sm, 1.6rem. Desktop section heads, the Up next row's titles, and the write-failure toast heading.

subhead.purpose: --text-bill-xs, 1.15rem. The wordmark and the compact phone deck titles. Also the phone hero's episode name at font-medium / leading-tight — the one ramp step used both with and without bill-title.

body.purpose: --text-note, 0.92rem. The synopsis at leading-relaxed capped at 68ch, and the running prose of the zero-match, empty and read-failure states at 60-62ch.

body-small.purpose: --text-item, 0.85rem. Episode names, the one-line 'what's next' under a grid entry, toast copy, and field text. Leading is inherited unless a leading-* class says otherwise.

fine.purpose: --text-fine, 0.7rem. Attribution and legal notices. One use in the build: the TMDB attribution pinned to the foot of the programme note.

label.purpose: 0.625rem at 0.16em tracking, wdth 100 / wght 600, uppercase. Baked into the code-line utility rather than declared as a token, so the code line is one size everywhere and cannot be resized at a call site.

motion.name: ease-press
motion.purpose: The only custom easing. Used by the strike sweep and the stamp landing.

motion.name: strike-sweep
motion.purpose: The 2px vermilion rule scaling in from the left across the episode name. transform-origin: left center.

motion.name: stamp-land
motion.purpose: The stamp scaling from 1.5 to 1 at a fixed rotate(-9deg). Off-register by design.

motion.name: hover-colors
motion.purpose: Tailwind's default transition-colors duration. Every hover in the system.

motion.name: press-brightness
motion.purpose: The recording control's active state, brightness(0.9).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the strike and stamp collapse to 1ms. The event still happens; it just does not animate.

themeTokens.usage: Page and panel ground; ink type on every inverted block; scrollbar track. Used with an opacity modifier as bg-ink/95 on the masthead.
hover:bg-ink-raised and the scaffolding panel's bg-ink-raised/80 only. The entire elevation vocabulary.
All display type and full-strength body type; the Caught up state label; ground of the selected nav item, selected filter chip, and active phone tab.
Metadata, code lines, synopsis, secondary state labels, inactive nav/chip/tab text, the abandon control, scrollbar thumb on hover. The most-used colour class in the build.
The 1px hairline; also as bg-rule under gap-px groups so the gaps themselves read as rules.
Structural division, field borders, the abandon control's underline, the scrollbar thumb, the toast's Dismiss border.
Consumed only through var(--color-spot) inside the plate utility. No *-spot class appears anywhere in the build — the ink is structurally unreachable except via the plate.
Live state, the recording control, the strike and stamp, focus ring, caret, selection, the selected rating, and every failure surface. Never the abandon control.
The programme note's title. Size only — no paired line-height token.
Phone TONIGHT heading, phone hero title, empty-library headline.
All twelve bill entry titles, plus the zero-match and read-failure headlines.
Desktop section heads (Tonight via lg:text-bill-sm, The library), the Up next row titles, the toast heading.
The wordmark, the compact phone deck titles, and the phone hero's episode name.
The synopsis (68ch) and the running prose of the zero-match (60ch), empty-library (62ch) and read-failure (62ch) states.
Episode names, the what's-next line under an entry, the Up next row's episode names, toast copy, the filter field and sort select.
One use: the TMDB attribution. Legal and attribution copy only.
Referenced as var(--font-display) inside the bill-title utility. The font-display class is never written.
Set once on body in @layer base. Same family as display — the two roles differ by width axis, not family.
A statement of intent that restates Tailwind's built-in. No rounded-* class appears anywhere in the build; zero radius is achieved by never applying one.
Referenced as var(--tracking-code) inside the code-line utility.
Referenced as var(--ease-press) in the plain-CSS strike and stamp transitions.

utilities.name: bill-title
utilities.declarations: font-family: var(--font-display); font-variation-settings: "wdth" 62, "wght" 900; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: -0.005em; line-height: 0.86;
utilities.purpose: Every title, at every size. Size is applied separately from the ramp (text-bill-md, text-bill-lg, ...).

utilities.name: code-line
utilities.declarations: font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: var(--tracking-code); font-size: 0.625rem; line-height: 1.1;
utilities.purpose: Every code line. Size is baked in, which is why 0.625rem is the one ramp step that is not a token.

utilities.name: plate
utilities.declarations: position: relative; isolation: isolate; overflow: hidden; background: var(--color-spot);
utilities.purpose: The duotone container. Its artwork filter and half-tone screen live in plain CSS (.plate > .art, .plate::after), because a @utility cannot reach a child or a pseudo-element.

typeRamp.note: Verified against the shipped file: no text-[...] class appears anywhere. An earlier build drifted to seventeen ad-hoc text-[Xrem] values; all seventeen are gone. Eight sizes are @theme tokens and the ninth (0.625rem) is baked into the code-line utility, so an off-ramp size cannot be written without inventing a class that does not exist. The closure is the deliverable, not the specific numbers.

absences: No spacing token — the build uses Tailwind's default 0.25rem step throughout.
No shadow or elevation token; box-shadow does not appear anywhere in the build.
No second palette, no light mode, no theme picker. One committed world, decided explicitly by the owner.
No line-height token. Leading is the bill-title 0.86, the code-line 1.1, or an explicit leading-* class; everything else inherits normal.
No *-spot utility class, so ultramarine is reachable only through the plate utility.
No rounded-* utility class anywhere, so radius is zero by construction rather than by convention.

rawHexExceptions.why: Content standing in for TMDB artwork, not palette.
Screen ink under mix-blend-mode: multiply, not a surface colour. Recorded as a detector exception in .impeccable/config.json.
A third party's colours, which are not ours to token.
The one place a palette value is repeated as a literal rather than read from --color-signal, because it sits inside an inline SVG fill. If the vermilion moves, this is the second place to change.

components.name: The Plate

narrative.overview:
MediaSafe is a season's programme, not a storefront. A repertory cinema prints one bill for the season: everything playing, in one ink, at one measure, with the house's own typography doing the work that a distributor's poster would otherwise do. The artwork serves the bill; it does not merchandise the title. This is the deliberate refusal of the thing every tracker ships — a rail of full-colour posters floating on near-black, where the interface is a shop window and the user is a shopper. Here the interface is a printed record of what one person is watching, and the record is the point.

The stock is a warm ink-black (#0E0D0B), never blue-black and never neutral #000; the type is bone (#E8E2D4), never pure white. Two spot inks are laid over that with fixed and non-negotiable jobs: ultramarine (#2740C8) as a solid field, and vermilion (#E85A38) as the one live signal. The discipline is structural, not remembered — ultramarine is consumed only inside the plate utility and no *-spot class exists in the build. Structure is hairline rules and inverted blocks, never boxes; there is no border radius and no shadow anywhere, and neither is an oversight. Depth comes from ink density and rules alone.

The type is set from a closed case: nine sizes, eight of them @theme tokens, with no arbitrary text-[Xrem] anywhere in the file. Titles are very large and very tight (condensed 900 at line-height 0.86) and metadata is very small and very wide (0.625rem at 0.16em tracking), with almost nothing in between. That gap is the composition, and it is the answer to the product's hardest constraint: this must never feel like a spreadsheet, and a table of same-sized rows is exactly what a spreadsheet is.

One committed world: no theme picker, no light mode, no alternate palette. color-scheme: dark is declared and the browser's own surfaces — selection, scrollbars, caret, focus ring — are painted from the same eight colours.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ink-black stock and bone type; no pure black, no pure white.
Two spot inks with fixed jobs: ultramarine is the only plate ink, vermilion is the only live signal.
One typeface (Archivo variable) at two widths — condensed 900 caps for names, normal-width 600 caps for code lines.
A closed type ramp: nine sizes, eight of them @theme tokens, and no arbitrary text-[...] class anywhere.
Zero border radius and zero shadows, system-wide.
Every borrowed poster is a duotone half-tone plate cropped to one fixed measure.
Hairline rules (1px, #2A2621) and 1px gaps over a rule-coloured ground are the only dividers.
Marking a watch is a material event — a strike and an off-register stamp, with the row's bounding rect unchanged.
Abandoning is the one hand-set state, and the quietest control on either surface.
One committed world: no theme picker, no light mode, no second palette.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Ultramarine is a field; vermilion is an event. Neither may do the other's job. Ultramarine is consumed only inside the plate utility and no *-spot class exists, so the rule is structural rather than remembered. If a new surface needs a third colour, it needs a different composition instead.

rules.name: The One Live State Rule
rules.body: Vermilion on a title means exactly one thing: you are in the middle of it. Watching is vermilion; Caught up is bone; Finished, Watchlist and Abandoned are dim bone. The state hierarchy is written in ink weight, and it never inverts.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text pair on the page passes WCAG AA, and the floor is 5.50:1 — vermilion on ink, and ink on vermilion. Measured on the live page: bone on ink 15.04:1, dim bone on ink 7.03:1, bone over the ultramarine plate 6.13:1. The vermilion was lightened to #E85A38 specifically to clear the 4.5:1 floor; a darker, more printerly vermilion failed it and was rejected. Do not darken it back.

rules.name: The Closed Ramp Rule
rules.body: Nine sizes, no tenth. Any size must come from the ramp; an arbitrary text-[Xrem] is a defect, not a tweak. An earlier build drifted to seventeen ad-hoc sizes, which is how a design system decays into a description of whatever got typed. If a new surface seems to need a size in between, it needs a different composition — or the ramp changes deliberately, in the @theme block, for everything.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: One family, two widths, no third register. If a piece of text is not a name (condensed 900 caps) it is a code line (normal-width 600 caps at 0.625rem / 0.16em) or it is body copy. Adding an in-between voice is how this world turns back into a generic app.

rules.name: The Named Episode Rule
rules.body: An episode is always its name. 'Hands', not 'S1 E2'. The number is a separate, dim code-line label set beside the name — never a replacement for it. No surface may degrade to a bare number, including the compact phone deck and the desktop Up next row.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeral Rule
rules.body: Anything carrying a number — years, networks, season and episode labels, the rating scale, reference ids — gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums via the [data-numeric] attribute. Numbers in a bill line up.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn, not spaced. Regions are separated by a 1px rule border, or by a 1px gap over a rule-coloured ground (gap-px on a bg-rule container) — never by whitespace alone, and never by a card with an outline and a radius.

rules.name: The Never-Navigate-Away Rule
rules.body: On desktop, inspecting a candidate replaces the programme note's contents and leaves the bill exactly where it was. Nothing about browsing your season should cost you your place in it.

rules.name: The Whole-Entry Rule
rules.body: A bounded row shows complete entries or nothing. The desktop Up next row is an auto-fill grid clipped to one row — as many whole entries as fit, never a partial card, never a scroller. Its max-height of 122px is keyed to the card's 92px plate plus 0.75rem padding; if the card's content grows, that number must be re-derived. The phone deck takes the opposite bound: no numeric cap at all, because a deck you work down never renders N at once.

rules.name: The Flat Stock Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, ever. If a surface needs to separate from what is behind it, give it a border, a solid ground, or one step of ink density — in that order.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Zero radius on every element, without exception. No rounded-* class appears anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Borrowed artwork is normalised to the programme's column, not the other way round. Whatever aspect ratio TMDB returns, the plate crops it to the fixed measure for that surface.

rules.name: The Material Event Rule
rules.body: Recording a watch strikes and stamps; it never turns a control blue, slides a switch, or removes the row from under the finger. The strike and stamp are absolutely positioned, so the row's bounding rect is identical before and after. The mark must look like something that happened to a printed sheet, and the row it happened to must not move.

rules.name: The Quiet Abandon Rule
rules.body: Abandoning is the one hand-set state in the model and must stay the quietest control on either surface: dim underlined text, no border, no fill, and never vermilion. Vermilion is reserved for recording a watch; giving up is not the daily gesture and must never compete visually with the one that is.

dos: Do keep ultramarine (#2740C8) as a field ink only — it is the plate, and nothing else. Keep it reachable only through the plate utility, so the rule stays structural.
Do keep vermilion (#E85A38) for live state, the recording control, the strike and stamp, focus, selection, and failure. Its scarcity is what makes it legible.
Do take every size from the closed ramp: nine sizes, eight tokens, zero text-[...] classes.
Do put every borrowed image through the plate: grayscale + contrast(1.12), mix-blend-mode: luminosity over spot, plus the 3px half-tone screen at .34.
Do crop artwork to the surface's fixed measure. The programme normalises everything to the column.
Do set names in condensed Archivo (wdth 62, wght 900, line-height 0.86) and everything administrative in the 0.625rem / 0.16em code line. Those are the two registers.
Do name episodes. 'Hands', with S1 E2 as a separate dim label beside it.
Do use the exact state vocabulary: Watchlist, Watching, Caught up, Finished, Abandoned.
Do keep the abandon control quiet — dim, underlined, unfilled, and never vermilion.
Do divide with 1px rules or 1px gaps over a rule ground.
Do invert to bone-on-ink or vermilion-on-ink when something needs to be the strongest thing on screen.
Do apply [data-numeric] (tabular figures) to anything containing a number.
Do pin the TMDB attribution to the foot of whatever pane shows borrowed data, out of the scroll.
Do keep the recording control in the thumb arc on phone, at the foot of the first screen.
donts: Don't add a border radius. Anywhere. 0px is the form language.
Don't add a box-shadow, a glow, a gradient scrim, or a lift-on-hover. Hover is ink to ink-raised and nothing more.
Don't write an arbitrary text-[Xrem]. That is how this build got to seventeen sizes; the ramp is closed and the closure is the point.
Don't show a poster in its own colours, at its own aspect ratio, or in a horizontally scrolling full-colour rail. That is the exact thing this world refuses.
Don't turn the desktop Up next row into a scroller, or let it render a partial card. It is bounded by the viewport; the remainder lives behind Library's Watching chip.
Don't put a numeric cap on the phone deck, or a 'showing 10 of 62' line. The deck's own form is the bound: 'A deck you work down — more load as you go'.
Don't use vermilion as a plate, an accent, a decorative hover, a brand flourish, or the abandon control, and don't darken it — #E85A38 is the value that clears the 4.5:1 contrast floor.
Don't use ultramarine for type, buttons, state, or emphasis, and don't introduce a *-spot utility class.
Don't introduce a third font, a third width, or a middle type size between the condensed name and the 0.625rem code line.
Don't build a theme picker, a light mode, or an alternate palette. This is one committed world.
Don't use pure #000 or pure #FFF. The stock is warm and the type is bone. The #000 in the plate's dot screen is screen ink under multiply, and is the one recorded exception.
Don't move, reorder, or remove a row when a watch is marked — strike and stamp in place.
Don't render dense tables, inline form fields, bulk-edit affordances, or admin chrome on an everyday surface.
Don't show a bare S3 E4 anywhere in place of an episode name.
Don't conflate Filter (your library) with Search (the catalogue) in any label.
Don't navigate away from the bill to inspect a candidate on desktop — replace the programme note's contents.
Don't document the fixed 'PROTOTYPE ONLY — STATES' panel as a component; it is scaffolding for exposing hidden states and has no place in the product.
